input.quote: (i) All paragraph headings contained in this Agreement are for convenience only and shall not affect the interpretation of this Agreement.
input.rationale: A full-text search for "insurance" returns nothing, and the General Matters section (§ 20 and its continuation, sub-clauses (a)-(j)) contains no insurance covenant. Garman performs on-site delivery, installation and data conversion at Sparkling's Authorized Locations and provides ongoing maintenance and support, so it touches both our premises and our data; the total absence of insurance is walk-away territory under the rule. We inserted the preferred coverage (CGL USD 1M/2M, E&O USD 2M, cyber USD 5M where our data is processed, workers' compensation, certificates on request) as a new sub-clause (k) in General Matters, noting the E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M fallback in the comment.

ops.text: (k) Garman shall maintain, at its own expense, throughout the term of this Agreement and for one (1) year thereafter: commercial general liability insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate; professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000; and, where Garman processes Sparkling's data, cyber liability insurance of not less than USD 5,000,000, together with workers' compensation coverage as required by law. Garman shall provide certificates of insurance to Sparkling on request.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We added a standard insurance covenant, as Garman personnel attend our locations and handle our data during installation, conversion and support. Our playbook expects CGL of USD 1M/2M, E&O of USD 2M and cyber of USD 5M with certificates on request; we can accept E&O of USD 1M and cyber of USD 2M if that better matches Garman's existing program.
proposal.summary: Insert vendor insurance covenant in General Matters
